To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The EGF receptor is overexpressed in 40% human brain tumour samples.
the expression of EGF receptor is frequently altered in primary human brain tumours and that there is no evidence for aberrantly expressed c-erbB2 in these tumours.
the EGF receptor is over-expressed in a proportion of primary human brain tumours, and this over-expression may be associated with gene amplification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the human brain tumor.
the role of growth factors and their receptors in the pathophysiology of human brain tumours and in particular the role of the epidermal growth factor receptor in glioblastomas.
the molecular basis of the malignant behaviour of human tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EGF receptor gene is amplified in some brain tumours but that the c-erb B-2 gene is not amplified or mutated in the brain tumour samples studied.
EGF receptor expression may be important in some brain tumours, and that c-erbB2 expression is probably of no significance.
the EGF receptor is expressed at high levels in 50% of human brain tumours and that this is associated with amplification of the EGF gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have not found any evidence of c-erbB2 gene mutations, amplification, or overexpression in human brain tumour samples.
the EGF receptor is a good marker of malignant potential, and that the EGF and PDGF receptor systems are important in the biology of human brain tumours.
EGF receptor expression is a common feature of brain tumours and that the EGF receptor gene is amplified in some cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found that there is an association between amplification and high expression of the EGR receptor gene in human brain tumour.
the expression of growth factor receptors is not restricted to the malignant cells in human brain tumour tissues.
EGF receptor is expressed at high levels in a subset of human brain tumours, and may be an important target for the development of new therapies for these tumours.
